Subject: CAIQ request: keystore rotation evidence + runtime trace samples

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the earlier call — Bluecrest is finalizing the vendor security review for our private deployment path and the review team asked for a compact CAIQ crosswalk that demonstrates how Redwood satisfies the controls around key management and rotation (we call this section KMS/HSM lifecycle). Specifically they need: 

- The CAIQ questions and your control responses that map to key rotation and key custody (we have a focused list of ~10 controls).
- Evidence of a recent key rotation (rotation event + audit log extract) and the rotation policy that governs scheduled rotations.
- A 72-hour sample of runtime traces showing key-access events and associated request IDs (redacted for sensitive data).

Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide and an ETA? We prefer a single zip with the crosswalk, rotation logs, and a short narrative explaining where the sample maps back to CAIQ control IDs.

Also note: Bluecrest needs guidance on redaction (PII removal) and an assurance that any traces we receive are safe to share with our internal auditors.

Appreciate it — can we aim for next-week delivery?

Best,
Sam Lin
Director, Security Engineering
Bluecrest Financial
[sam.lin@bluecrest.com]

High level deliverables we will prepare: 
- CAIQ control crosswalk (compact spreadsheet) that maps Redwood control responses to the specific CAIQ questions you flagged.
- Key rotation policy & attestation (PDF): covers rotation cadence, roles, and HSM/KMS usage.
- Rotation event log export (CSV) showing RotateKey/ImportKey events with timestamps and key IDs (we will provide key identifiers hashed).
- Runtime trace sample (72 hrs) with request IDs tokenized; we will remove all customer payloads and PII.
- A short narrative (1 page) that points to which artifact proves each CAIQ assertion.

ETA and next steps: 
- Priya will run the export and redaction job. Expect an initial package within 5 business days (by Fri, 30 Apr). If you need accelerated turnaround we can prioritize but will require a short uplift approval.

Hi Sam — Priya here. Quick note on the artifacts and a brief description of redaction and formats so your audit team can prepare: 

What we'll include (file list):
- caig_crosswalk_bluecrest_20270427.xlsx (compact crosswalk, includes control IDs and short evidence pointers; see column "evidence_path").
- keystore_rotation_history_20270401.csv (fields: timestamp, event_type, key_id_hash, actor, region). key_id_hash is SHA256 of the internal key ID; we will provide the salt used in the narrative so you can match if needed.
- runtime_trace_sample_72h_redacted.zip (contains per-day trace files; each line is a JSONL event with tokenized_request_id, event_type, kms_action). All payload fields and user identifiers are removed.
- ksm_attestation_20270427.pdf (signed attestation from our Key Custody lead confirming rotation and HSM usage).

Redaction / privacy notes: 
- We will remove any customer content and user identifiers. The runtime traces will retain request IDs (tokenized) and timings so auditors can follow event chains.
- Audit-log timestamps are in UTC; we'll include a small script (sha mapping.txt) that maps key_id_hash -> rotation window if you need cross-referencing.

Mapping approach to CAIQ: 
- We'll include a brief mapping table where our internal control label (e.g., KRM-ROT-01) points to CAIQ control ID(s) and the specific evidence file/line. Example: KRM-ROT-01 -> CAIQ-CCM-KEY-03 -> keystore_rotation_history_20270401.csv (line 42).

Access & delivery: 
- Package will be uploaded to a shared Drive folder; we can provision time-limited access.
- If Bluecrest requires execution of an NDA / additional DPA scoping for traces, please send the DocuSign link.

ETA: Friday, 30 Apr EOD (tentative) — ping me if you need earlier.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Control Evidence Lead, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
